sections.heading: C — Impairment effects and preparing to drive
sections.markdown:
## C — Impairment effects and preparing to drive

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
Marijuana affects both thinking skills, such as judging and planning, and physical skills, such as coordination, reaction time and tracking, so driving while impaired by it raises the risk of death or injury. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
How impaired marijuana makes you depends on the dose, the time since use, the individual, and the way it was consumed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
Unlike alcohol, the amount of THC measured in blood, breath or saliva does not track how impaired a person actually is. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
Colorado law allows a permissible inference of DUI when a driver has 5 nanograms of THC per milliliter of blood. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
There is no THC inference level for DWAI, and most marijuana-impaired drivers are convicted on their behavior together with blood THC results. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
Polydrug impairment means using two or more drugs at once, in any mix of alcohol, marijuana, prescription, over-the-counter or other drugs, and the mix can strengthen the effects. [A01]
Why it matters: Colorado data on the cited page calls it more common than any single drug except alcohol, and more dangerous.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A01
Illegal drugs such as LSD, methamphetamine and heroin harm reflexes, judgment and alertness, and can either create false confidence or leave you too drowsy to react. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A01
Officers are trained to recognize and testify about impaired driving from any cause, and drivers are convicted regardless of which drug was involved or how much was found in blood or saliva. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A01
Under the Express Consent Law (C.R.S. 42-4-1301.1), driving in Colorado means you have agreed to a chemical test for alcohol or drugs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A01
When an officer suspects impaired driving, you can be required to give a blood, breath, saliva or urine sample for testing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A01
Refusing or failing to cooperate with the chemical test leads to a one-year license revocation plus a two-year requirement to use an ignition interlock on any vehicle you drive. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A01
An ignition interlock requires a breath sample before the engine starts and repeat samples while driving, and the vehicle will not start if it detects elevated alcohol. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A01
Any other suspension or revocation from the same incident is added after the refusal revocation ends, served consecutively. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A01
Penalties for alcohol or drug driving offenses are severe and can include jail, fines and loss of driving privileges. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A01
Colorado does not allow plea bargaining an alcohol or drug driving offense down, so the only sure protection is never driving after using alcohol or drugs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A01
Safe driving requires clear vision, being rested, being sober and drug-free, general good health, and mental and emotional fitness, while using all your senses to notice danger. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A01
Good vision is essential because you drive on what you see; have your eyes checked by a specialist every year or two. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A01
If your license carries a corrective lens restriction, you must wear your glasses or contacts whenever you drive. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A01
Being able to hear does not guarantee you will notice outside sounds, since music, talking passengers or a well-insulated car can mute them, and hearing can decline slowly with age or noise. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A01
You may not drive wearing earphones, meaning any device that covers all or part of both ears. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A01
Hearing aids, cochlear implants, assistive listening devices, speakers built into protective headgear, and a single-ear wireless device do not count as earphones. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A01
Fatigue slows reactions and decisions, so split long drives into two-hour segments and pull off the road to rest if you get drowsy. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0008]
